title: Which triangles hide in two circles through each other's centres?
description: Two circles of the same size pass through each other's centres, and the places where they cross are joined to the centres. The radius shows which triangles have three equal sides and which have two.
teaching_notes: One idea: a crossing place of two circles is the radius away from both centres. Watch for children who find only the triangle on top and miss the matching one below.

source: Two circles of the same size have centres A and B, and each passes through the centre of the other; then three such circles. Form isosceles and equilateral triangles.
video_script.why: The child has seen that the crossing of two arcs is the right distance from both centres and now finds triangles in two whole circles.
video_script.substitution: The two circles have the same radius, and that radius is the distance between their centres.
video_script.anchor: Two circles of the same size, each passing through the centre of the other, and then three such circles
video_script.payoff_line: Triangles eigh B C and eigh B D are equilateral.

final_answer.value: ABC and ABD equilateral; ACD and BCD isosceles; with three circles ABC equilateral
final_answer.spoken: triangles eigh B C and eigh B D are equilateral, and eigh C D and B C D are isosceles

hold_back: Triangles ABC and ABD are equilateral
never_show: the names of the equilateral triangles before the answer beat
maths_rules: each circle passes through the other's centre, so the radius r = AB
C is on the circle at A, so AC = r = AB; C is on the circle at B, so BC = r = AB; AB = BC = CA, so ABC is equilateral
D likewise: AD = BD = AB, so ABD is equilateral
AC = AD (radii of the circle at A), so ACD is isosceles; BC = BD (radii of the circle at B), so BCD is isosceles
three circles: every pair of centres is one radius apart, so ABC is equilateral
video_script.design: One idea: a crossing place is the radius away from both centres. The two circles stay in the anchor band; the working band holds the board solution.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Triangles ABC and ABD are equilateral; ACD and BCD are isosceles; with three circles, ABC is equilateral
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Triangles eigh B C and eigh B D are equilateral.
Triangles eigh C D and B C D are isosceles.
<bookmark mark='three'/>With three circles, the triangle of the three centres is equilateral.
